semantics: Queue lock precedes the event-handle lock; event code does not call back into the queue.
Enqueue signals the event and wakes blocking high-level consumers. Both nonblocking and blocking pops clear the event only when the shared queue becomes empty.

Messages queued before the first event query retain their FIFO order. Initial status follows them.
Fixed queue capacity remains 32; overflow now fails explicitly instead of silently dropping a notification.
One writable event is retained for process lifetime. Readable-copy reference counts and handle slots are reclaimed by the existing real CloseHandle SVC.
